report.headline: Supabase is an open-source Postgres development platform providing database, authentication, APIs, edge functions, and storage for web, mobile, and AI applications.

positioning.summary: Supabase positions itself as a comprehensive Postgres development platform, offering a suite of integrated backend services as an open-source alternative to Firebase. It emphasizes ease of use, scalability, and the power of a full Postgres database.
positioning.targetCustomer: Product developers building web, mobile, and AI applications, from passion projects to large-scale, internet-scale workloads.
valueProps: Every project is a full Postgres database, known for being trusted, portable, and extensible.
Offers built-in authentication with Row Level Security.
Enables easy custom code execution with Edge Functions without server deployment.
Allows storage, organization, and serving of large files.
Facilitates building multiplayer experiences with real-time data synchronization.
Integrates with ML models for vector embeddings storage, indexing, and search.
Provides a unified dashboard with Table Editor, SQL Editor, and RLS Policies for managing applications.
Offers production-ready templates for quick project kickstarts.
differentiators: Strong affinity for open-source maintainers and ex-Founders in the team.
Offers self-hosted Deno functions with Edge Runtime.

pricing.summary: Supabase offers a tiered pricing model that includes a generous free tier, escalating to Pro and Team plans with increasing features, resources, and support, and an Enterprise plan for large-scale needs.
pricing.model: Per-project subscription with usage-based billing for additional resources (MAUs, disk size, egress, file storage) beyond included limits.
pricing.freeTier: Free plan includes unlimited API requests, 50,000 monthly active users, 500 MB database size, shared CPU/500 MB RAM, 5 GB egress/cached egress, 1 GB file storage, and community support. Projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity. Limit of 2 active projects.

tiers.name: FREE
tiers.notes: Perfect for passion projects & simple websites. Paused after 1 week of inactivity. Limit of 2 active projects.

tiers.name: PRO
tiers.notes: Most popular, for production applications. Includes everything in Free, plus higher limits, email support, daily backups (7-day retention). Additional projects from $10/mo.

tiers.name: TEAM
tiers.notes: Adds features like SSO, control over backups, SOC2 & ISO 27001 certifications, project-scoped access, HIPAA as add-on, priority email support & SLAs, daily backups (14-day retention), 28-day log retention. Additional projects from $10/mo.

tiers.name: ENTERPRISE
tiers.notes: For large-scale applications with internet-scale workloads. Includes custom designated support manager, uptime SLAs, AWS PrivateLink support, 24x7x365 premium enterprise support, private Slack channel, custom security questionnaires.

techStack.summary: Supabase's tech stack suggests a modern, performance-oriented, and open-source-centric development team. The use of TypeScript for core projects like `supabase`, `mcp`, and `cli`, along with Next.js for their frontend, indicates a strong focus on developer experience and efficient web development. The use of Elixir for `realtime` and Rust for `etl` demonstrates a commitment to high performance, concurrency, and reliability in specific critical components, typical of a mature and well-funded engineering organization tackling complex backend challenges.

signals.name: TypeScript
signals.evidence: Used in supabase/supabase, supabase/mcp, supabase/cli GitHub repositories

complaints.summary: The main complaint identified is a significant security vulnerability that could lead to database leaks, though it appears to have been publicly disclosed and likely addressed.

items.complaint: The Supabase MCP (Postgres metadata proxy) could leak entire SQL databases.
items.source: Supabase MCP can leak your entire SQL database - Hacker News

recentMoves.summary: Supabase has been very active, raising substantial funding rounds, expanding its platform capabilities with S3-compatible storage and enhanced real-time features, and hosting developer events. A significant security vulnerability was also disclosed and likely addressed.

items.move: Raised $500 million Series F funding round at a $10.5 billion valuation.
Active development on core GitHub repositories (supabase, realtime, mcp, cli, etl).
Raised $100 million Series E funding at a $5 billion valuation.
Disclosure of a vulnerability where Supabase MCP could leak entire SQL databases.
Raised $200 million Series D funding at a $2 billion valuation.
Supabase Storage now supports the S3 protocol.
There was a public discussion and blog post about migrating from Supabase, indicating some users may find reasons to move away from the platform.
Launched Supabase Edge Runtime for self-hosted Deno functions.
Launched Supabase (YC S20) as an open-source Firebase alternative.

opportunities.summary: Supabase's rapid growth, broad feature set, and high valuation present opportunities for competitors to target specific niches, address documented pain points, or offer differentiated experiences.

items.gap: Despite broad offerings, users might find it complex or overwhelming for very specific use cases.
items.why: The platform aims to be a comprehensive "Postgres development platform," which might lead to feature bloat for simple needs.
items.howToExploit: Offer a hyper-focused, single-purpose backend service (e.g., just auth, or just real-time) that is significantly simpler and easier to use for that specific function, potentially at a lower entry cost or with a more generous free tier for that narrow scope.

items.gap: The 'Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity' policy could be a deterrent for hobbyists or long-term personal projects that are not constantly active.
items.why: This policy, while likely designed to manage resource costs, can frustrate users who are not actively developing but want their projects accessible.
items.howToExploit: Provide a truly 'always-free' tier for small, inactive projects, perhaps with very limited resources, but without the pausing mechanism. This could attract hobbyist developers who might eventually scale up and migrate to paid plans.
